chunks: And from him, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'The concubine of a man nursed a boy, and he has a daughter from another wife. Is it permissible for that boy to marry this daughter?' He said: 'I dislike for a man to marry the daughter of a man whose son has nursed from his milk.'

key_terms.أُمُّ وَلَدٍ: Concubine (a slave woman who bears her master's child)

ai.seo_question: Does a concubine's daughter become a milk-sister to her master's son if she nurses him?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the status of marriage between a milk-brother and the daughter of his wet nurse, stating he dislikes the union. This reflects the Shia scholarly view that while the bond creates a mahram relationship, the prohibition may be rooted in strong dislike (karāhah) or specific conditions of the nursing, distinguishing it from the absolute prohibition of blood siblings. The hadith underscores the importance of milk kinship (radāʿ) in establishing familial ties and marriage restrictions within the extended family structure.
